name: Bone broth, chicken
evidence: Chicken bone broth has gone mainstream: Target alone carries at least five brands including Swanson (a legacy, near-universal soup-aisle brand) with full pickup/delivery options. This makes 'most' a confident floor; it may well be 'everywhere' but Aldi/Costco/Walmart/Kroger couldn't be individually confirmed this session, and Aldi in particular tends to favor its own private-label broth which may or may not be marketed specifically as 'bone broth.' Retailers checked: Walmart: unverified this session (tool budget exhausted) - Swanson is a near-universal Walmart soup-aisle brand by general knowledge, though not tool-confirmed today; Kroger: unverified this session, same caveat; Target: in-store (multiple brands confirmed: Kettle & Fire, Swanson, Pacific Foods, Bare Bones, Butcher's Bone Broth, plus Good & Gather store-brand chicken broth, all with shipping/same-day delivery/in-store pickup/order pickup); Aldi: unverified - unclear whether Aldi's private-label broth line includes a distinct 'bone broth' SKU (as opposed to regular broth/stock); no evidence found either way this session; Costco/Sam's: unverified. everywhere_substitute: Regular chicken broth or stock (Swanson or any store brand), confirmed at essentially every US grocery chain including Aldi. Regular broth has meaningfully less protein per serving than true bone broth (bone broth is simmered longer for collagen, roughly 8-10g protein/cup vs. standard broth's 1-2g/cup) - this materially changes the satiety/protein role the food plays in a plan, so it isn't a clean swap; flag to the coach rather than substitute silently. https://www.target.com/s?searchTerm=chicken+bone+broth
unverified: Walmart, Kroger, Aldi, and Costco/Sam's could not be individually checked this session (WebSearch budget exhausted mid-task).
everywhere_substitute_short: low-sodium chicken broth (less protein)

name: Arepa (cornmeal bread)
evidence: REVIEW (tier kept): Specialty for most of the US. Note: the South Florida stores checked DO carry them (Walmart #2946 (Davie FL) live check: El Latino/Kiosco arepas, P.A.N. and Goya masarepa; ALDI Cooper City FL live check: P.A.N. corn meal), which reflects that area's Venezuelan/Colombian community, not the national assortment. Target: one small frozen SKU, no masarepa (research). || RESEARCH: Both ready-made arepas and masarepa/arepa flour are specialty items for most of the US. Target — a broad big-box chain — carries only one small-brand frozen ready-made arepa and zero masarepa/P.A.N.-style flour products; Goya (an otherwise near-universal Latino-foods brand) makes a masarepa product, but it did not surface at Target, implying it is carried mainly by stores with a strong Latin American foods section (larger Kroger/Publix/H-E-B locations, Latino markets) rather than nationally. Retailers checked: Walmart: unverified; Kroger: unverified; Target: in-store but very limited (one SKU: El Sembrador Frozen Arepa de Choclo, a small regional Latino brand; no masarepa/P.A.N.-style flour found); Aldi: unverified; Costco/Sam's: unverified; other: unverified. Sources: Target's only ready-made arepa result is 'El Sembrador Frozen Arepa de Choclo, 12oz/2ct' ($5.69, 'Highly reordered', SNAP EBT eligible, available for pickup/same-day delivery) (https://www.target.com/s?searchTerm=arepas) | Target search for masarepa/arepa flour returns no P.A.N. or masarepa product — only unrelated all-purpose/gluten-free flours and Maseca corn flour (a tortilla/tamale masa, not masarepa) (https://www.target.com/s?searchTerm=masarepa+arepa+flour) | Target search for Goya-brand arepa/masarepa or P.A.N. returns no matching products; only unrelated Goya seasonings, rice, beans, and frozen plantains (https://www.target.com/s?searchTerm=goya+arepa) | Goya's own website lists 'Masarepa' as a featured product, confirming Goya makes an arepa-flour product even though it did not surface at Target (https://www.goya.com/en/products?q=arepa)

name: Salmon, Atlantic wild, cooked
evidence: REVIEW (tier kept): Not sold commercially in the US at all (wild Atlantic salmon fishing is closed; every Atlantic salmon for sale is farmed) per NOAA sources in research. A client told to buy 'wild Atlantic salmon' cannot. || RESEARCH: This USDA nutrient-database record has no real-world commercial match in the US. Wild sea-run Atlantic salmon fishing (commercial and recreational) has been illegal since the species was federally listed as endangered, so every 'Atlantic salmon' sold anywhere in the US -- big-box, supermarket, or high-end online fishmonger -- is farmed, and every product labeled 'wild salmon' is a Pacific species (sockeye, pink, keta, coho, king). name: Swiss chard, cooked
evidence: Confirmed in-store at Kroger, H-E-B, Albertsons and Safeway (all real product pages). Walmart and Target show a genuine gap - fresh chard did not surface even after multiple targeted searches, unlike every other vegetable in this batch, which suggests it's a weaker item for the two biggest mass-market chains specifically. Combined with Aldi being called out as unreliable, 'most' (full-size traditional supermarkets yes, big-box/discount format less certain) is the best-supported tier. Retailers checked: Walmart: not confirmed as fresh produce - repeated searches (including a '-seeds -plant' filtered search) surfaced only Swiss chard seed packets and Bonnie Plants starter plants, not a fresh bunch for eating; Kroger: in-store (Swiss Chard Green Bunch and Organic Red Swiss Chard - own kroger.com listings); Target: not found via search (searches for 'swiss chard' and 'chard' both returned unrelated cheese/snack products - likely a search-indexing gap rather than confirmed absence); Aldi: inconsistent (a shopper on MetaFilter's 'How to Aldi' thread specifically cautions that going in for something like Swiss chard may result in disappointment); Costco/Sam's: not found this session; other: in-store at H-E-B (own heb.com listing) and at Albertsons/Safeway (own product pages for Organic Swiss Red Chard). Sources: Kroger's own product pages for Swiss Chard Green Bunch and Organic Red Swiss Chard (https://www.kroger.com/p/swiss-chard-green-bunch/0000000004586) | H-E-B's own product page for Fresh Organic Red Swiss Chard (https://www.heb.com/product-detail/fresh-organic-red-swiss-chard/374991) | Albertsons' own product page for Organic Swiss Red Chard (https://www.albertsons.com/shop/product-details.184710336.html) | Safeway's own product page for the same Organic Swiss Red Chard (https://www.safeway.com/shop/product-details.184710336.html) | Repeated Walmart searches surface only seeds/plants, not fresh chard for eating (https://www.walmart.com/c/kp/swiss-chard-lucullus) | Target search for 'swiss chard' returns cheese products, not the vegetable (direct page fetch) (https://www.target.com/s?searchTerm=swiss+chard) | Shopper caution that Aldi may not have specific items like Swiss chard on a given trip (https://ask.metafilter.com/271441/How-to-Aldi)
everywhere_substitute: Baby spinach (fresh bagged). About as close to universally stocked as a leafy green gets - appeared as a 'related item' across nearly every Target produce search performed in this research (arugula, okra, artichoke searches all surfaced Good & Gather spinach), and is standard at Walmart, Kroger, and Aldi. Very similar low-calorie leafy-green profile (chard cooked is 20 kcal/1.88g protein per 100g per the spec; cooked spinach is roughly comparable, ~23 kcal/2.9g protein/100g by general reference values, not independently re-verified this session). Minor difference, not material. https://www.target.com/s?searchTerm=arugula
unverified: Costco/Sam's not checked. Whether Walmart/Target genuinely lack fresh chard in-store, versus their websites simply under-indexing fresh leafy greens (a pattern seen elsewhere in this research), could not be resolved with the remaining tool budget.

name: Vegan kimchi
evidence: REVIEW (tier kept): Walmart #2946 (Davie FL) live check: Pulmuone Spicy Vegan Kimchi in store. ALDI Cooper City FL live check: no kimchi. Costco's main brand is not vegan (research). || RESEARCH: A specifically vegan-labeled kimchi (not just 'kimchi' generally) is directly confirmed by name at Walmart, Kroger and Target, and at Whole Foods/Publix (Wildbrine). Costco's main brand is traditional (fish sauce/shrimp), and Aldi's vegan-kimchi status is unclear, so a shopper is not guaranteed a vegan option at every store the way they are for kimchi in general. Retailers checked: Walmart: in-store; Kroger: in-store; Target: in-store; Aldi: unverified; Costco/Sam's: not found (dominant brand there is not vegan); other: Whole Foods/Publix/Safeway in-store (Wildbrine). Sources: Walmart.com sells 'Lucky Seoul Vegan Kimchi, 14 oz Jar' and 'Lucky Foods Kimchi... probiotic, vegan, keto certified' by name (https://www.walmart.com/ip/Seoul-Refrigerated-Vegan-Kimchi-14-Oz/483840601) | Kroger.com sells 'Nasoya Spicy Vegan Cabbage Kimchi' as a named, regularly stocked product (https://www.kroger.com/p/nasoya-spicy-vegan-cabbage-kimchi/0002548400740) | Target.com sells 'Seoul Vegan Spicy Kimchi - 14oz' and 'Seoul Vegan Original Kimchi - 14oz' as Non-GMO Verified, Gluten-Free named products (https://www.target.com/p/seoul-vegan-spicy-kimchi-14oz/-/A-54598802) | Whole Foods Market sells Wildbrine Kimchi and Mother-in-Law's Vegan Napa Cabbage Kimchi, both fish-free; Publix.com lists Wildbrine Kimchi Probiotic Korean Style (https://www.publix.com/pd/wildbrine-kimchi-probiotic-korean-style/RIO-PCI-558767) | A shopper review reports Costco's dominant kimchi brand, Jongga, 'had the traditional fish sauce / shrimp flavor' -- i.e. not vegan -- with no vegan-labeled Costco kimchi identified (https://www.tiktok.com/@lovekoreanfood/video/7210789035894164779?lang=en)
everywhere_substitute: Sauerkraut (raw, live-culture) or regular (non-vegan) kimchi if the client isn't strictly vegan. Same fermented-vegetable, probiotic, tangy-crunchy role in a bowl or side; raw sauerkraut is naturally vegan and widely stocked (see separate sauerkraut entry). Sauerkraut is very similar macro-wise to kimchi (19 kcal/0.9g protein/100g vs kimchi's 15 kcal/1.1g protein/100g) so this swap barely changes plan macros
brand_hint_note: Regular kimchi is also only most-tier (the ALDI checked had no kimchi at all); vegan-labeled kimchi (e.g. Pulmuone Spicy Vegan) was on the shelf at the Walmart checked.
unverified: Could not confirm a specifically vegan-labeled kimchi at Aldi or Costco; 'Simple Truth Raw-Fermented Kimchi' (Kroger) and Aldi's 'Plant Menu Kimchi Pieces' vegan status were not verified from ingredient labels.
